A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAVIA/SAVID research. All main-text and appendix material is readable and supports comparison. V1's discounted algorithms move into Section 4.2, while its Appendices C and D become B and C in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports algorithms, theoretical complexity comparisons, and mathematical proofs, including Appendices A–D. It contains no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical throughout the main text and Appendices A–C. Its expanded comparison table reports analytical bounds from the literature, not empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Anchoring, recursive sampling, sampling schedules, doubling, and stopping thresholds are retained for SAVIA/SAVIA+ and SAVID/SAVID+. Algorithm 5 explicitly passes the already-defined discount factor gamma in v2; this repairs an omitted argument without changing the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts empirical training or evaluation. Average-reward and discounted MDPs remain the theoretical settings.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. The additional methods in Table 1 broaden the literature's theoretical complexity comparison, rather than an evaluated baseline set.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports an experimental evaluation protocol, data splits, training budgets, or testing procedures. Algorithmic sampling parameters are specifications for the theoretical analysis.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablation studies, robustness experiments, sensitivity tests, or empirical case studies. The revised appendix arguments are mathematical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the theoretical high-probability and expected-complexity framework.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries or measured findings appear in either version. Changes to symbolic complexity bounds and literature comparisons are assessed under T1 and R1.

T1.justification: V2 expands Proposition 4.1's proof and adds intermediate complexity derivations in Theorems 3.4 and 3.6, retaining the principal rates and assumptions. It also revises logarithmic prefactors: Theorem 3.4 replaces log^4(2(1+mu/epsilon)) with ln^4(1+mu/epsilon), which vanishes at the permitted case mu=0. The new Theorem 3.6 derivation removes conditioning on the stopping index without justification.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central algorithm and near-optimal complexity claims. Section 1.1 broadens the novelty comparison beyond model-free methods: v1 singles out Jin et al. (2024a), while v2 identifies Tuynman et al. (2024) as the previous fully prior-knowledge-free method and emphasizes SAVIA+'s broader applicability.

C2.justification: Section 1.3 more precisely distinguishes running without unknown parameters from choosing a sufficient budget and certifying termination. Section 3.1 drops v1's specific fifth-order characterization of naive sampling. The discounted worst-case gap and proposed multichain and online extensions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm 5 corrects its inner SAVID call by explicitly including gamma, omitted in v1 despite being part of the method's signature. No code, data, hardware, or resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: Table 1 and Section 1.3 substantially broaden positioning to model-based and model-free algorithms, organized by MDP class and three prior-knowledge requirements. Zurek and Chen (2025) is newly cited; previously cited methods receive expanded comparisons. Tuynman's applicability changes from weakly communicating to communicating MDPs. Li et al. (2024)'s displayed complexity dependence changes from t_mix^2/epsilon^3 to t_mix^3/epsilon^2.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized revisions to the introduction, related-work discussion, and selected proofs, adds a Prior knowledge paragraph heading and acknowledgments, and moves discounted-algorithm descriptions into Section 4.2. The overall narrative and section sequence remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 1 is substantially redesigned with expanded citation-based rows, method-type and MDP-class columns, three groups of prior-knowledge requirements, and a rewritten caption. Algorithms 4 and 5 move from full-width appendix displays to main-text columns.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the precision of research positioning and makes Proposition 4.1's reasoning more explicit. However, the revised Theorem 3.4 prefactor produces a zero complexity bound at allowed mu=0, and the added Theorem 3.6 step drops conditioning without justification. These local rigor regressions accompany clearer exposition, while the main contributions remain stable, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
